blocks.heading: Telecommunications LLM Applications
paragraphs: AT&T (Dallas HQ), AT&T's network technology operations, and Texas's dense telecommunications infrastructure create specific LLM applications:

Customer service and billing AI: LLM-powered customer service for AT&T's massive subscriber base — natural language billing inquiries, service troubleshooting, and plan comparison at the scale that AT&T's contact center operations require.

Network operations documentation: RAG over AT&T's enormous technical documentation corpus — enabling network engineers to query equipment specifications, troubleshooting procedures, and network topology documentation in natural language.
Competitive intelligence synthesis: LLM systems synthesizing telecommunications competitor announcements, regulatory filings, and network performance data for AT&T's strategic planning teams.
Cost: $30,000–$90,000 | Timeline: 10–20 weeks

blocks.heading: Financial Services LLM Applications
paragraphs: Goldman Sachs (major Dallas campus), JPMorgan Chase (major Dallas technology campus), Capital One, and Texas Capital Bank:

Risk and compliance documentation: LLM generating first-draft regulatory submissions, model risk narratives, and compliance documentation from structured data inputs for DFW's large financial services operations.

Investment research synthesis: RAG-powered research assistants for Goldman's and JPMorgan's Dallas-based analysts — querying earnings transcripts, SEC filings, and market intelligence across large document sets.
Commercial lending documentation: LLM processing commercial loan applications, generating credit memo drafts from financial statement data, and extracting covenant compliance information.
Cost: $30,000–$90,000 | Timeline: 10–20 weeks

paragraphs: $20,000–$90,000 for most DFW enterprise LLM integrations. Healthcare and financial services applications with compliance logging at the higher end.

blocks.heading: "How long does LLM integration take in Dallas?"

blocks.heading: "Texas doesn't have strict consumer privacy laws — does that simplify LLM compliance?"
